exposure: Frozen repair plan and its primary adjudication read. No lead returned-image verdict supplied. Primary observations preserved unchanged.
phone_note: Actual390x844 history screenshots show complete R landscape artwork at338x225.33 and15-C1 portrait at338x507. These are slightly smaller than360px primary gallery art. No owner controls or selection changes occurred in the captures.

observations: R still shows only four separated feet: three near-side supports and one far-side support. Native and phone both fail to reveal the other two required legs.
Mint stone body, shovel face, slab load and quiet outlined treatment persist. Camera/body framing changes do not establish a material topology gain.

Retain P with explicit unresolved six-leg requirement; neither P nor R should be certified as six-legged. Choosing P is preservation in the absence of the intended repair, not a claim P meets the contract.
All four complete feet now separate against lighter ground, with three broad rounded pads visibly present on each foot. The previously hidden far rear foot is exposed.
The low glass gecko, cyan eyes, single tapering tail and crisp faceted rendering persist; facet clutter reduces without becoming a different creature.
Phone supports four-foot counting more readily than P. Cyan internals and tail sparks remain busier than a strict simplified-plane design, but do not hide the feet.
Harness, red straps, brass fitting and green tool are removed. The elongated rear foot/tail-like protrusion is also removed, leaving one round tail and a cleaner body.

Two forefeet, one broad near hindfoot and a smaller far hindfoot under the belly can be identified at native size. The far hindleg attachment remains hidden and its foot becomes subtle on phone; fully exposed four-limb attachment is not established.

Expressive face, huge blue leaf ears and warm outlined ceramic painting remain cohesive. R materially clarifies the intended inventory and reduces the extra-form ambiguity without erasing creature identity.
Four separate orange cloth sail sectors now radiate from one axle, with all tips inside frame; three appear intact and the lower-left sail is visibly torn.
Complete rotor, approaching storm mass, turquoise tower, access door and stair path remain legible on phone. The camera pullback is a material repair to mechanism comprehension.
Tower and hatch are smaller than P and torn cloth remains largely held by its frame rather than freely hanging onto the route. These limits do not undo the clear four-sail framing gain.
Floating sheets now read as blank pale paper with physical edges and minimal texture; the prior printed/ruled rows no longer appear on that raft.
Two shelf banks, bright raised route, open door, black flood and pink tabs retain the same useful scene organization in the actual phone image.

Dry-brush marks and reflections vary across the edited raster, so this is not an assertion of exact unchanged pixels outside the raft. Dense shelves still compress at phone scale, without a new focal obstruction.
The mallet now has a broad cylindrical head mounted crosswise to its short shaft, with a long side and one round end visible; its T construction matches the actual15-G1 gear more clearly than P.
Thumb/fingers still wrap the handle, with a short shaft length between hand and head. Native and phone preserve the older face, heavy adult build, open explaining palm and complete feet.
Dense engraving remains coherent. Dark head against the dark coat has modest contrast at phone size, but its crosswise silhouette is legible; no new prop or conspicuous anatomy defect appears.

remaining_limits: 17-M1 has four visible feet in both P/R despite six required.02-M1 far hindleg attachment remains occluded. Earlier54-primary deviations remain disclosed; five recommendedR are not owner acceptance or whole-study conformance.
